subject: Post-call: POC network & egress ownership checklist
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Erin Jacobs <erin@finmetrics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: POC network & egress ownership checklist

Hi Erin — great call today, thanks for walking us through FinMetrics' privacy requirements and the initial staging topology. Per our discussion, attaching a concise checklist for the POC networking decisions so we can lock scope before the workshop. High-level recap:

- FinMetrics prefers a Private VPC deployment to keep inference traffic within a controlled network (good).
- Two connectivity options on the table: AWS PrivateLink (endpoint service) vs VPC Peering. You signaled a preference for PrivateLink due to cross-account segmentation and auditability.
- Outstanding: egress ownership for model downloads and telemetry (who manages NAT / proxy for outbound internet access), and exact IP allowlist required for our control plane and S3 model pulls.

Next steps I captured from the call:
1) FinMetrics to confirm whether outbound internet for model updates will route through your central egress proxy or you want Redwood to stage a NAT/proxy in the VPC.
2) You to provide a minimal allowlist for a POC (CIDR or single IP ranges preferred) — we can support both static IPs (for Dedicated) and ranges for PrivateLink.
3) Schedule a 60-min network workshop (NetOps + Security + Redwood SEs) — suggested times below.

Attachments: quick POC checklist and a reference architecture image.

I put Marissa and Ben on CC to own the workshop prep and IP matrix. Thanks —

Dylan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0132
From: Erin Jacobs <erin@finmetrics.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: POC network & egress ownership checklist

Dylan — thanks for the clear recap and the checklist. Quick clarifications from our side before the workshop:

1) Egress ownership: We prefer to keep outbound internet egress owned by FinMetrics' central cloud team. That means: model downloads (S3), telemetry, and any outbound webhook calls should flow through our egress proxy (bluebox-proxy-01) so we can apply perimeter DLP and logging.

2) IP allowlist for Redwood control plane: we can provide two /28 ranges for the POC; final production requests will need static IPs or a PrivateLink approach. Can you confirm whether PrivateLink requires additional route table changes on our side vs simple endpoint creation?

3) TLS and KMS: we will need confirmation that Redwood can integrate with our KMS for key wrapping (customer-managed keys) and that the Private VPC deployment will still allow key rotation mechanics.

We can do the workshop Thursday 10/15 10:00–11:00 PT or Friday 10/16 14:00–15:00 PT.

Erin
Director, Cloud Engineering | FinMetrics
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Erin Jacobs <erin@finmetrics.com>, networking@finmetrics.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: POC network & egress ownership checklist

Erin — perfect, thanks for the clarity. Short answers up front:

- PrivateLink vs Peering: PrivateLink is primarily endpoint-service oriented and avoids route table exposure between accounts; you create an interface endpoint in your VPC and we register our service. Peering creates a direct route table connection; it's simpler but gives broader VPC access. For your security posture, PrivateLink aligns better. It will require you to create an interface endpoint and allowlist our service; no route table edits beyond the usual security group updates.

- Egress (model downloads & telemetry): Agreeable — if FinMetrics manages outbound via bluebox-proxy-01, Redwood will route model fetches through that proxy during the POC. For that we need proxy hostname/IP and the proxy's allowed outbound ports (typically 443). If you prefer Redwood-managed NAT for the POC, we can provision a small NAT instance in a staging subnet (but that would place egress responsibility on Redwood and require SOC2 evidence for our infrastructure).

- KMS: We support customer-managed KMS integration for key wrapping on the Private deployment. We'll need a brief IAM role mapping and key policy draft. Key rotation semantics are supported; we'll coordinate with your security team during the workshop.

Action items before the workshop (we'll own items 1 & 3):
A) FinMetrics: send minimal POC allowlist (/28s are fine), proxy hostname/IP, and preferred workshop attendee emails.
B) Redwood (Marissa & Ben): produce an IP-by-service matrix (control plane, model fetch, telemetry) and an example PrivateLink endpoint acceptance test.

I'll schedule the workshop for Thu 10/15 10:00 PT — invite forthcoming.

Best,
Dylan
